Chittor taken 1303; southern campaigns 1307–1311 1336, 1347 Foundation of Vijayanagara and of the Bahmanī sultanate 1398 Tīmūr sacks Delhi 15th c.  Firearms appear in Indian warfare 1498 Vasco da Gama reaches Calicut 1518 Maḥmūd II of Malwa restored with Gujarati help; the Purbiya soldiers driven from Mandu 1526 First battle of Pānīpat; Bābur founds the Mughal empire 1528 Bābur storms Chanderi, held by the Purbiya chief Medinī Rāy 1536 The Ahoms sack the Kachari capital, Dimapur c. 1562–1563 Koch invasion of the Ahom kingdom under Cilārāy 1565 Battle of Talikota (Rakshasa–Tangadi) 1567–1568 Akbar’s siege of Chittor 1576 Battle of Haldighati 1595–1596 Chand Bībī’s defence of Ahmadnagar 1600 Execution of the fourth Kuñjāli Marakkār 1659 Śivājī kills Afzal Khān at Pratapgad 1671 Ahom victory over the Mughals at Saraighat 1674 Coronation of Śivājī 1681–1707 Aurangzeb’s wars in the Deccan c. 1698–1729 Kānhojī Āṅgre, Maratha admiral 1699 Guru Gobind Singh institutes the Khalsa 1734 Hastividyārṇava completed in Assam 1742–1751 Maratha (bargī) raids into Bengal 1748 Sikh fighting bands act together as the Dal Khālsā 1757 Battle of Plassey 1761 Third battle of Pānīpat 1763 Mīr Qāsim of Bengal, with his new regular battalions, defeated by the Company 1764 Battle of Buxar 1767–1799 Anglo-Mysore wars; Mysore rockets; Srirangapatna falls 1799 1768–1769 Gorkha conquest of the Kathmandu valley 1784 Benoît de Boigne enters the service of Mahādjī Shinde 1788–1792 Wars between Nepal and Tibet; a Qing army enters Nepal (1792) 1798 The Nizam’s French-officered corps disbanded under a subsidiary alliance 1799–1839 Ranjit Singh’s kingdom of Punjab 1801 Awadh cedes about half its territory to the Company 1803 Battle of Assaye c. 1804 Congreve’s rocket experiments in Britain, influenced by Mysore rockets 1808–1809 Rising of Vēlu Tampi against the Company in Travancore 1814–1816 Anglo-Nepal war; Treaty of Sugauli 1815 The Company begins to recruit Gurkhas after the surrender at Malaun; the British annex Kandy in Sri Lanka 1817 Paika rising in Odisha 1817–1818 Pindārī and Third Anglo-Maratha wars; Khadki, Sitabuldi, Mahidpur, Koregaon 1822 Allard and Ventura enter Ranjit Singh’s service 1824 Rising of Cennammā of Kittūr 1826 Treaty of Yandabo: Burma renounces Assam, Manipur, Cachar and Jaintia 1831–1832 Kol rising in Chota Nagpur 1834–1841 Zorāwar Siṅgh’s campaigns in Ladakh, Baltistan and western Tibet 1843 Miani and Dubba (Sindh); Maharajpur and Panniar (Gwalior) 1845–1849 Anglo-Sikh wars 1855–1856 Santal rising (hul) 1857–1858 The great rising; death of the Rāṇī of Jhānsī 1878 Indian Arms Act 1888–1889 Imperial Service Troops of the princely states instituted 1899–1900 Birsa Munda’s rising (ulgulān) in Chota Nagpur 1911 Indian soldiers become eligible for the Victoria Cross 1914–1918 About 1.3 million Indians serve in the First World War 1932 Indian Military Academy opens at Dehradun 1939–1945 The Indian Army grows to about 2.5 million 1946 Mutiny of the Royal Indian Navy at Bombay and other ports 1947 Independence and Partition; docs.title: Glossary
docs.text:
Terms are Sanskrit unless marked (Ta. = Tamil, Mal. = Malayalam, Pe. = Persian, Hi. = Hindi/Hindustani, Ma. = Marathi, Pu. = Punjabi, Mn. = Meitei/Manipuri, Ka. = Kannada).

Term Meaning akhāṛā (Hi.) Wrestling ground and gymnasium; also an armed division of an ascetic order akṣauhiṇī In the Mahābhārata, the largest army unit (21,870 chariots and elephants, 65,610 horse, 109,350 foot) ālīḍha A wide lunging stance, in the Agni Purāṇa with the right leg held rigid; also a posture of iconography amukta A weapon held in the hand and not released, e.g. the sword (in the Agni Purāṇa’s classes of fighting) āpaddharma Law or duty in time of distress, when ordinary rules may be relaxed ari The enemy; in the circle of kings, the neighbouring king Arthaśāstra Treatise on statecraft attributed to Kauṭilya; composite, c. 50 BCE–300 CE astra A missile weapon; in the epics, a divine weapon released by spell aṭavī Forest people; forest troops recruited by kings āyudhapūjā Worship of weapons and tools on the ninth day of Navarātri bāgh nakh (Hi.) “Tiger claws”, a concealed clawed weapon worn in the palm bārgīr (Ma./Pe.) Trooper riding a horse supplied by the state or his commander batta (Hi.) Extra allowance paid to Company troops for field service or service outside the Company’s territory bhṛta Hired or mercenary troops brahmāstra The most powerful divine weapon of the epics caturaṅga “Four-limbed”: the army of chariots, elephants, cavalry and infantry; the ancestor of chess cit (Hi.) In wrestling, a fall with both shoulders on the ground daṇḍa The rod; coercive power, punishment; the army; also the “staff” battle array daṇḍanīti The science of government and punishment daṅgal (Hi.) A wrestling tournament dhāl (Hi.) Round shield dhanurveda “Knowledge of the bow”; the science of arms dhanus Bow dharmavijaya Righteous conquest, in which the defeated ruler is reinstated as tributary dharmayuddha Righteous war; war fought according to rules durga Fort fauj-i-āʾīn (Pe.) “The army of rules”: the regular army of the Sikh kingdom firangī (Hi.) Straight sword, often with a European blade in an Indian hilt fitna (Pe.) “Sedition”; the winning over of an opponent’s followers as a technique of politics gadā Mace gaja, hastin Elephant ganimī kāvā (Ma.) The Maratha style of mobile, irregular warfare gatkā (Pu.) Stick-fencing; the Sikh martial art gurukkaḷ (Mal.) Master of a kaḷari iqṭā (Pe.) Assignment of revenue to a military commander in the Delhi Sultanate jāgīr (Pe.) Assignment of land revenue to a Mughal officer in lieu of salary jaidād (Pe.) Revenue assignment for the support of troops, e.g. that of the Shinde brigades in the Doab jamādār (Pe./Hi.) Leader of a band of soldiers; later a junior Indian officer jauhar (Hi.) Collective self-immolation of women in a besieged fort kaḷari (Mal.) Training ground of kaḷarippayaṟṟu kaḷarippayaṟṟu (Mal.) The martial art of Kerala kampū (Hi.) A brigade of regular troops in Maratha service (usually derived from Portuguese campo, “camp”; the derivation is not certain) kaṭār (Hi.) Push-dagger with a transverse grip kavaca Armour khaḍga Sword khaṇḍā (Hi.) Straight broad double-edged sword kṣatriya Member of the warrior and ruling class of the varṇa order kūṭayuddha Concealed war: surprise, ambush and stratagem kushūn (Pe.) A brigade of Tipu Sultan’s army kuśtī (Pe./Hi.) Wrestling malla Wrestler mallakhamb (Ma.) Gymnastics on a vertical wooden pole or rope maṇḍala Circle; the circle of kings in foreign policy; a battle array manṣab (Pe.) Rank in the Mughal service, expressed in zāt and sawār numbers marma Vital point of the body; marmmam (Mal.), varmam (Ta.) misl (Pu.) A confederacy of Sikh fighting bands in the eighteenth century mitra Ally mukta A weapon that is thrown or released; the Agni Purāṇa distinguishes weapons released by a machine such as the bow (yantramukta) from those released by the hand (pāṇimukta) naukar, naukarī (Pe./Hi.) Servant; service, especially military employment nāyaka Military chief holding territory from the king (Vijayanagara) paik Footsoldier; in Assam, a man liable to service under the Ahom state palṭan (Hi.) A battalion of regular infantry (usually traced to English “battalion”; “platoon” has also been proposed) pañjī In the warfare of the North-East, a sharpened bamboo stake planted in paths and approaches paṭā (Ma./Hi.) Gauntlet sword patti, padāti Infantry; foot-soldier pindārī (Hi.) Irregular horseman living by plunder, attached to or independent of the Maratha armies prakāśayuddha Open war puṟam (Ta.) “Exterior”: classical Tamil poetry of war and public life pūrbiyā (Hi.) “Easterner”: soldier from Awadh, Banaras or Bhojpur rākhī (Pu.) “Protection”: the share of produce paid by villages to a Sikh misl ratha Chariot sāma, dāna, bheda, daṇḍa The four means (upāya): conciliation, gifts, dissension and force ṣāḍguṇya The six measures of foreign policy saptāṅga The seven constituents of the state sarkhel (Ma.) Admiral of the Maratha fleet senāpati Commander of the army śastra A weapon held in the hand silambam (Ta.) The staff-fighting art of Tamil Nadu śiledār (Ma.) Trooper who owned his horse and arms and hired them out with his service skandhāvāra Military camp sūta Charioteer talwār (Hi.) Curved sabre with a disc pommel thang-ta (Mn.) “Sword and spear”; the armed martial art of the Meitei tūṣṇīṃyuddha “Silent war”: covert action and assassination by secret agents uṟumi (Mal.) Flexible sword of Kerala vajramuṣṭi Combat with a knuckle-weapon; the weapon itself vijigīṣu “Would-be conqueror”; the king at the centre of the circle of kings vīrakal (Ka.) Hero-stone, memorial to a warrior vīrāṅganā Heroic woman; woman warrior vyāyām (Hi.) Exercise; physical culture vyūha Battle array wootz Indian crucible steel (from Kannada and Telugu ukku) yantra Machine, including machines of war
